title: Scout C3: where a pre-execution spec review plugs in (role, prompt, hold, test approach)
spec:
HARD OUTPUT CAP: JSON under 4,500 chars; ≤10 findings; evidence path:line only. Read-only.
Read: orchestrator/bus.py ROLES and create_task; orchestrator/spawn.py run_worker prompt selection per role and the review path (review verdict capture); .orchestrator/prompts/review.md, scout.md, challenge.md; orchestrator/mcp.py spawn_review/spawn_challenge; skills/review/adversarial-review/SKILL.md. Answer: (1) minimal way to add a spec review: new role "spec_review" in ROLES with a prompts/spec-review.md template (inputs[0] = the execute task id; the reviewer reads that task's spec, acceptance, scope and the current code at the scoped paths, and returns {"verdict":"approve|request_changes","risks":[{"path":"","issue":"","severity":""}],"suggested_spec_changes":[...]}) vs reusing role review with a flag — cite the code that would change either way; (2) where the hold lives: bus task status "held" with hold_reason "spec_review pending" set at creation for complexity ≥5, cleared by the daemon or Planner on approve — cite the fields; (3) how run_worker should write the verdict onto the execute task (spec_review_verdict) like review_verdict does; (4) an mcp tool spawn_spec_review(task_id) mirroring spawn_review; (5) test approach without spawning claude: FakeProc pattern in tests (Executor tests) — cite it. suggested_next: file list with insertion points.
acceptance: role/prompt/hold/verdict/tool insertion points cited with path:line
test approach cites the existing FakeProc pattern

findings.claim: Minimal path: add 'spec_review' to ROLES set and a prompts/spec-review.md; role dispatch in run_worker needs a new elif branch mirroring the review branch (which reads inputs[0] as the reviewed task id and renders diff/acceptance)

Alternative: reuse role='review' with a flag (e.g. inputs[0] flagged as spec vs diff) avoids touching ROLES/TOOLS/create_task validation, but forces render() and the verdict-write branch to branch internally on task metadata instead of role, which is messier than a new role given render() already dispatches by name string

STATUSES already includes 'held'; hold_reason is not a declared task field in create_task's dict but is set dynamically via bus.update(**fields) kwargs, exactly as spawn.py does for 'no account with headroom' and rate_limit holds

For a spec_review hold at creation (complexity>=5), create_task would need a status='held' + hold_reason override since it currently hardcodes status:'queued' at bus.py:55; simplest is to call bus.update(new_task['id'], status='held', hold_reason='spec_review pending') right after create_task rather than modifying create_task's signature

Verdict is written onto the target execute task inside run_worker's post-processing: role=='review' checks result.get('verdict') and calls bus.update(task_id, review_verdict=...) plus bus.update(inputs[0], review_verdict=...) on the reviewed task; a spec_review branch would mirror this with spec_review_verdict
mcp.py exposes spawn_review as a thin @srv.tool() wrapping the shared _bg(task_id) background dispatcher; spawn_spec_review(task_id) would be an identical 3-line addition calling _bg(task_id)

review.md prompt template shows the shape a spec-review.md would need: static instruction + {{complexity}}/{{security}} + task content placeholders ({{diff}} becomes spec/acceptance/scope) + a fixed 'Return ONLY JSON' contract line

Tests avoid spawning real claude/codex by monkeypatching executor.subprocess.run with a FakeProc(stdout, returncode) stand-in for CompletedProcess, restored via addCleanup; the same pattern (patching subprocess.run in the relevant module) applies to testing a spec_review worker path

run_worker's role dispatch for review already special-cases inputs[0] as a string task id to fetch a worktree/branch context before rendering, which is the same access pattern a spec_review reviewer would use to read the execute task's spec/acceptance/scope and scoped code

open_questions: Exact complexity threshold enforcement point (create_task caller vs a hook) for auto-holding new execute tasks pending spec_review isn't in bus.py/spawn.py — likely lives in Planner-side task-creation flow, not scouted here
Whether TOOLS dict (spawn.py:8) needs a new 'spec_review' entry for allowed tool access — not fully inspected
suggested_next: orchestrator/spawn.py:8 add TOOLS['spec_review'] entry (copy 'review' entry, read-only)
orchestrator/spawn.py:191-197 add elif role=='spec_review' branch rendering .orchestrator/prompts/spec-review.md with spec/acceptance/scope/code-at-scope
orchestrator/spawn.py:215-219 add elif role=='spec_review' writing spec_review_verdict via bus.update on both task_id and inputs[0]
tests/test_orchestrator.py: new Executor-style test using FakeProc (line 83) to fake the spec_review worker run and assert spec_review_verdict lands on the execute task
